Word: ὁ ὢν καί ὁ ἦν καί ὁ ἐρχόμενος
Transliteration: ho ṑn kaí ho ēn kaí ho erchómenos
Definition: a phrase combining G3588 with the present participle and imperfect of G1510 and the present participle of G2064 by means of G2532; the one being and the one that was and the one coming, i.e. the Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ:--which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be).
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
